clue.text: Arrived at front of theatre, appearing in small role

indicators.note: something appearing in a production is placed inside it, so one piece goes inside the other
'front of' keeps only the first letter of 'theatre'

blocks.note: the first letter of theatre
a cameo is a brief walk-on part, often for a star

explanation.surface: An actor turns up at the theatre entrance to play a bit part.
explanation.walkthrough: A cameo is a well-known actor's brief walk-on appearance; the theatre's initial lands just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to a place is a phrasal verb for reaching it, so 'came to' swaps for 'arrived at'.

clue.text: As part of goal, negotiate hazard at sea

blocks.note: to negotiate an obstacle is to get across it
a bar is a sandbank that blocks a harbour mouth

explanation.surface: A sailor's instruction to get past a danger on the way to port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goal' sounds like a destination for the voyage; it is the football frame.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossbar is the horizontal beam across the top of a football goal, one of its parts.

clue.text: Variety of vermin linked to a Roman deity

indicators.note: a variety is a different form of something, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kind of pest associated with a god of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linked to' reads as a link but here joins vermin to the a that completes the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Minerva was the Roman goddess of wisdom, equivalent to Greek Athena.

clue.text: One who afflicts people residing between hills

indicators.note: something residing between two things lives in the middle, so it sits inside

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor; two of them here
men are people

explanation.surface: A villain who torments the inhabitants of a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN sits between two TORs. A tor is a craggy hilltop, common in the south-west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is someone who causes suffering, which is what afflicting others means.

clue.text: Fellow mostly using few words in sections of text

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for few words is dropped

blocks.note: chap is an informal word for a man
terse speech is brief and clipped

explanation.surface: A man who says little is described as dividing up a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapters are the numbered divisions of a book, which is a body of text.

clue.text: Fashionable river vessel makes diversion for semiaquatic creatures

blocks.note: hip means trendy
the Po is Italy's longest river
a pot is a container
to amuse is to divert or entertain

explanation.surface: A trendy riverboat offers entertainment for water-loving animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a boat, especially beside 'river', but it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippos spend their days in rivers and lakes and graze on land at night, so they are semiaquatic.

clue.text: Devout leaders from parish insist on usual service

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: the initials of the five words

explanation.surface: Religious heads of a parish demand the familiar form of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Pious means religiously devoted and reverent, a synonym of devout.

clue.text: Ring-leader in bar is a piece of work

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter of ring is used
in places the selected letter inside the word for bar

blocks.note: bar as a preposition means except, as in 'all bar one'
the first letter of ring

explanation.surface: The ringleader of a gang drinking in a pub is a troublesome character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring-leader' reads as one word for a gang boss; split it. R goes into EXCEPT: EXCE-R-PT. 'a piece of work' suggests a nasty person; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is an extract, a piece taken from a longer piece of writing or music.

clue.text: Display or conceal test for illness

blocks.note: first meaning: to show a film or programme
second meaning: to hide behind a partition
third meaning: to check people for a disease

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings: two of them are near opposites, show and hide.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to show on a screen, to shield from view, and to examine people for disease.

clue.text: Searching TV for sporting action between us and France?

definitions.text: sporting action between us and France?

blocks.note: first meaning: flicking through the stations with a remote

blocks.clueFragment: sporting action between us and France?
blocks.note: second meaning, whimsical: riding waves on the strait between England and France

explanation.walkthrough: The English Channel separates Britain ('us') from France; riding the waves there is a joking literal reading of the TV phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means hopping from one television station to another, and literally a water sport in the strait.

clue.text: Possession arranged with person losing little time

indicators.note: losing tells us that something is taken away from the letters gathered
arranged means put into a new order, so the gathered letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something owned is set out in agreement with a person who is running short of time.
explanation.walkthrough: WITH plus PERSON lose a T, leaving WIH and PERSON to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ownership is the state of having something as your own, which is what possession means.

clue.text: Award that comes after November, as heard on radio

definitions.text: that comes after November, as heard on radio

blocks.note: first meaning: the statuette given by the film Academy

blocks.clueFragment: that comes after November, as heard on radio
blocks.note: second meaning: the code word for O, following the word for N in the radio spelling alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: The NATO phonetic alphabet used by radio operators runs ... Mike, November, then this word for O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award statuette is nicknamed the same as the radio code word for the letter O.

clue.text: Boy harbouring desire to become skilled operator

indicators.note: to harbour something is to shelter it inside, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: a son is a male child
an urge is a strong desire

explanation.surface: A lad nurses an ambition to be a skilled professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operator' suggests machinery or switchboards; here it is someone who performs operations.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon performs operations, so 'skilled operator' is a playful description of the medical role.

clue.text: Keep watch, say

blocks.note: first meaning: to watch closely
second meaning: to remark or comment

explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes 'say' look like 'for example'; it is a verb meaning remark.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to watch attentively and to make a remark, as in 'he observed that it was late'.

clue.text: A carriage reversed away from others

indicators.note: reversed tells us to read the word for a carriage from back to front

blocks.note: taken as written
a trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: A coach is backed out of the line, separated from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand apart is to be separate and at a distance from the rest.

clue.text: Antagonism about some soldiers produces outrage

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hostility word goes around the soldiers

blocks.note: enmity is hostility or antagonism
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Hostility towards a group of troops leads to public anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Other ranks' are the soldiers below officer level, a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An enormity is a grave crime or wicked act, an outrage in the sense of a shocking deed.

clue.text: Powerful female's case not finished within month

indicators.note: not finished means the end is missing, so the last letter of the word for case is cut
within means inside, so the shortened word sits in the month

blocks.note: a case in court is a trial
taken as a month of the year

explanation.surface: A strong woman's legal case remains unresolved inside a month.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIAL loses its last letter and TRIA goes into MARCH: MA-TRIA-RCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is a woman who heads a family or group, a figure of authority.

clue.text: Provide meal that includes meat cooked in dramatic fashion

indicators.note: something that includes another holds it inside, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: to feed someone is to give them a meal
lamb is a kind of meat

explanation.surface: Instructions for serving a dinner with meat prepared theatrically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meat' and 'meal' both suggest the food itself, but the cooking style is the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambéed dish has spirits poured over it and set alight at the table, a showy way of cooking.

clue.text: State in which banks are corrupted

indicators.note: corrupted means spoilt or altered from its proper form, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A comment on a place where the financial institutions have gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' does double duty, both in the fodder and as the verb before the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska is one of the fifty US states, in the Great Plains.

clue.text: Learned English — unrefined without it

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
rude can mean crude or unpolished
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Englishman who is coarse and lacking sophistication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but in its old sense means outside, so the second word surrounds the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned, said as two syllables, means scholarly and well read, which is what erudite means.

clue.text: Fired back, hemming in American Indian

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for fired the other way round
hemming in means enclosing on all sides, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: lit means set on fire, ignited
AM is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Someone shoots back, trapping a Native American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American Indian' reads as one phrase, but American is wordplay and Indian alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamils are a people of southern India and Sri Lanka, so a Tamil is an Indian.

clue.text: Berth in sound by Jersey or Guernsey before storm

blocks.note: Jersey and Guernsey are breeds of dairy cow, and a cow's call is a moo
to storm is to rage

explanation.surface: A boat's mooring off the Channel Islands as bad weather comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey and Guernsey look like the Channel Islands, which suits a harbour; here they are the cattle breeds named after them.
explanation.definitionFit: A moorage is a place where a boat can be tied up, which is a berth.

clue.text: Sailor dispatched somewhere else

blocks.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
sent means dispatched

explanation.surface: A sailor posted to another location.
explanation.definitionFit: To be absent is to be away and not present, so in another place.

clue.text: Checker at entrance challenging delivery

blocks.note: first meaning: a doorman who vets people entering a club
second meaning: in cricket, a short ball that rears up at the batsman

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler's delivery is the ball bowled; one pitched short so it rises sharply at the batsman has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a nightclub doorman and a short-pitched cricket ball that rises towards the batsman.

clue.text: Caught river fish put in here

definitions.text: Caught river fish put in here

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
R is the abbreviation for river
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Where an angler stores the fish just landed from the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer while its first three words build it.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket in which anglers keep the fish they have landed.

clue.text: Level in educational establishment for male

blocks.note: uni is short for university
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Reads like a standard of attainment at a single-sex school.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform as an adjective means the same throughout, even and unvarying, which is what level means.

clue.text: Centrepiece of candlelit events for exclusive group

indicators.note: the centrepiece is the middle portion, so the letters come from inside the run of words

blocks.note: the letters straddling the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A table decoration at candlelit functions is reserved for a select few.
explanation.walkthrough: candl-ELIT E-vents.
explanation.definitionFit: An elite is a select, privileged group set apart from the rest.

clue.text: Make drunk mix it in a beer

indicators.note: to mix things is to stir them together, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A barman's instruction to spike a beer to get someone tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: To inebriate someone is to intoxicate them, a formal verb for making drunk.

clue.text: Those people having put old record in priest's study

indicators.note: having something put in means it is placed inside, so the pronoun word holds the others

blocks.note: they refers to those people
O is the abbreviation for old
a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: People storing an old document in a clergyman's room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' looks like a room in the vicarage; it is the subject a priest studies.
explanation.definitionFit: Theology is the academic study of God and religion, which a priest trains in.

clue.text: Guard started crossing line

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so one word sits across and around the other

blocks.note: a horse that shied started back in alarm
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A sentry began walking across a boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'started' looks like began; here it means jumped in fright, as a horse shies. SHIE-L-D.
explanation.definitionFit: To shield something is to protect it, a synonym of guard as a verb.
